artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define the map T : ℤ_{>0} → ℤ_{>0} by
   T(n) = n/2          if n is even,
   T(n) = (5n+3)/2     if n is odd.
For a positive integer n, write Ω(n) for the (finite) cycle of T containing n when its forward orbit is periodic, and let C(5,3) denote the set of all such cycles of T on ℤ_{>0}. For each cycle Ω(n) let G(n) := { m ∈ ℤ_{>0} : the forward T-orbit of m eventually enters Ω(n) }, and let G(∞) := { m ∈ ℤ_{>0} : the forward T-orbit of m is unbounded }.

Consider the seven explicit cycles
  Ω(1)  = (1 → 4 → 2 → 1),
  Ω(3)  = (3 → 9 → 24 → 12 → 6 → 3),
  Ω(39) = (39 → 99 → 249 → 624 → 312 → 156 → 78 → 39),
  Ω(43) = (43 → 109 → 274 → 137 → 344 → 172 → 86 → 43),
  Ω(51) = (51 → 129 → 324 → 162 → 81 → 204 → 102 → 51),
  Ω(53) = (53 → 134 → 67 → 169 → 424 → 212 → 106 → 53),
  Ω(61) = (61 → 154 → 77 → 194 → 97 → 244 → 122 → 61).

Prove or disprove the following:
(a) C(5,3) = { Ω(1), Ω(3), Ω(39), Ω(43), Ω(51), Ω(53), Ω(61) };
(b) ℤ_{>0} = G(1) ⊔ G(3) ⊔ G(39) ⊔ G(43) ⊔ G(51) ⊔ G(53) ⊔ G(61) ⊔ G(∞);
(c) G(∞) ≠ ∅.
artifact.status_search_result: The 5n+3 Syracuse variant is a known generalization of the Collatz problem; the original 3n+1 conjecture remains open, and no published resolution of the cycle-classification or divergent-orbit conjectures for the 5n+3 variant was found. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Collatz conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: One of the most famous unsolved problems in mathematics... Matthews and Watts proposed conjectures about generalizations.
status_evidence.claim: The Collatz problem and its generalizations (such as the 5n+3 variant) remain open.

status_evidence.title: On a general Syracuse problem with conjectures
status_evidence.snippet: General Syracuse problem with conjectures including the 5n+3 case.
status_evidence.claim: The cycle-classification statement for the 5n+3 map is posed as a conjecture.
